clue.text: We're DPs -judge us without expression of surprise

parts.note: a referee, REF for short, judges a match

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the pieces for judge and us wrap round the exclamation

parts.note: taken as written
gee! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Displaced people plead with a judge not to show any astonishment at their case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. DPs is short for displaced persons, a post-war term; 'We're' simply introduces them.
explanation.definitionFit: Displaced persons are people forced from their homes, which is what the word for asylum-seekers and exiles describes.

clue.text: Admiral's aim, to turn up among half of Royals

indicators.note: among means the reversed piece sits inside the other
half of keeps the first three of the six letters
in a down clue turning up reads the word from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A naval commander's goal is to appear among half of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' Royals gives ROY; END, 'to turn up', becomes DNE, placed 'among' it. George Rodney was an 18th-century British admiral.
explanation.definitionFit: George Brydges Rodney was a British naval commander famous for victory at the Saintes.

clue.text: Educational expedition for starters, followed by dance

parts.note: the field is all the starters in a race
to trip is to dance lightly, as in trip the light fantastic

explanation.surface: A school outing begins with a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' looks like 'first letters', but the field is the starters in a race. 'followed by' sets TRIP after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A school outing to study something on site is an educational excursion.

clue.text: Inferior cigars, given time, could be affecting digestive system

indicators.note: inferior cigars are poor ones, badly made, so their letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Cheap cigars, smoked long enough, could upset the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inferior' signals the anagram of CIGARS plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for the stomach describes something to do with digestion.

clue.text: People involved in the old rising (the other side)

indicators.note: in a down clue rising reads upwards, so the letters go backwards
involved in means one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: ye is the old form of the
men are people

explanation.surface: People caught up in a historic uprising join the opposing camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' wraps the people in the old word, and 'rising' then turns the result upward, giving YMENE read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Your opponents in a war or contest are the hostile party.

clue.text: Drum with reddish fruit leaving a mark

indicators.note: the fruit is leaving a letter behind, so one piece is taken out of the word

parts.note: a tomato is a red fruit
the letter A is the piece removed
M is short for the mark, the former German currency

explanation.surface: A drum is stained by squashed red fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' tells you TOMATO drops its A, giving TOMTO; M for mark completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a tall narrow drum beaten with the hands.

clue.text: It no doubt helps to pull a blade

definitions.text: It no doubt helps to pull a blade

parts.words: It no doubt helps to pull a blade
parts.note: blade suggests a sword or knife, but here it is the flat end of an oar, held while a rower pulls

explanation.surface: Something that helps draw a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowlock holds the oar in place as a rower pulls it.

clue.text: Catches end of broadcast on box, having turned over

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word
turned over means the boxing word is read backwards

parts.note: to box is to spar

explanation.surface: A broadcast ends on the TV box, which then flips over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' broadcast gives T; SPAR, 'having turned over', becomes RAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Snares that catch animals; as a verb, both mean to capture.

clue.text: Fellow crewman seems upset about flat

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, or around, the next piece
upset means the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: mat or matt describes a flat, dull finish

explanation.surface: A shipmate looks disturbed about his cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the five letters to MESSE, which 'about' wraps round the flat word. 'flat' is not a home here but a dull finish, as in matt paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors who eat together in the same mess are dining companions aboard.

clue.text: Oil for massaging sore knee

indicators.note: massaging works the letters over until they take another shape

explanation.surface: Oil rubbed into a painful knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'massaging' signals the anagram of SORE KNEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is a fuel oil distilled from petroleum.

clue.text: Occasions when those taking part get into gear

definitions.text: Occasions when those taking part get into gear

parts.words: Occasions when those taking part get into gear
parts.note: get into gear reads as starting to work hard, but here the cast literally put on their costumes

explanation.surface: Events where the participants finally get going.
explanation.definitionFit: Final run-throughs of a play in full costume are when actors first put on their stage clothes.

clue.text: Early English line about Lord getting on

indicators.note: about tells you the first pieces go round the next one

parts.note: EE is the abbreviation for the Early English style of Gothic architecture
RLY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: An early English line of verse concerns an ageing aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LD inside EE + RLY, between the two Es. Early English is a phase of English Gothic church architecture, abbreviated EE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting on is advancing in years, that is, old.

clue.text: Name of animal, nothing I can read in Latin

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
possum is the Latin for I am able

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they cannot read Latin at all, while naming an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: POSSUM is Latin for 'I can', so 'I can' read in Latin gives it, after O for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The American marsupial that plays dead is named by this word.

clue.text: A keg crew found floating in debris from vessel?

indicators.note: loose things floating about are not fixed in place, so these letters drift into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors and a keg are found adrift among the remains of a sunken ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floating' signals the anagram of A KEG CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left of a wrecked ship is its broken remains; the question mark says vessel is just one example.

clue.text: Camel's point of departure could be warm -remove clothing

parts.note: to air clothes or a room is to warm and dry them
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A camel sets off when it could be hot enough to undress.
explanation.walkthrough: The Camel is the Sopwith Camel, a First World War fighter plane, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A biplane takes off from a landing strip, its point of departure.

clue.text: Knight captures a pawn, not working

annotationWithheld.why: Knight captures a pawn, not working (5): K (or KT) plus A and P gives no U; the clue as held lacks the piece giving U and no print found restores it
annotationWithheld.clue: Knight captures a pawn, not working

clue.text: Pole's article on Church of England, maybe

parts.note: a perch is a pole, an old measure of length
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Polish man writes about the Anglican church, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person, but it is a perch, a measuring rod.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb meaning possibly, perhaps.

clue.text: Watch host almost coming to grief in TV programme

indicators.note: coming to grief means wrecked, so the letters fall into a new order
almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: Watch a presenter nearly fall apart on a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' takes host to HOS; 'coming to grief' rearranges WATCH + HOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A television format where a presenter interviews guests is a talk show.

clue.text: Intensively publicised sample of starchy pedantry

indicators.note: sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A taste of stuffy fussiness is overpromoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sample of' shows the answer sits inside starcHY PEDantry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something promoted with heavy publicity has been given a lot of hype.

clue.text: Luncheon recess?

parts.note: recess reads as a break for lunch, but here it is an alcove, a nook where meals are eaten

explanation.surface: A lunch break.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dining nook in a kitchen is an alcove used for eating.

clue.text: Send out again for story about divorced wife

indicators.note: the story goes about, or around, the former partner

parts.note: a news report is a story
an ex is a former spouse

explanation.surface: Someone sends out another account about their former wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the former wife inside the story, straight after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods shipped abroad again after being imported are sent out once more.

clue.text: Shrine visitor turning cheek, resolute

indicators.note: turning means the word for cheek is read backwards

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk
grim means determined

explanation.surface: A visitor to a holy place turns the other cheek with determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses LIP to PIL. 'cheek' is impudence, not the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim travels to a sacred place as a devotee.

clue.text: Notice woman's last to use stick

parts.note: an ad is a notice
her is the word for a woman's

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A notice asks the final woman to use some glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woman's' gives HER (possessive), and 'last' to use gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling or be glued to something is to stay attached.

clue.text: Superior decoration featured on locks

parts.note: superior means on the very top, and locks means hair rather than door fastenings: a bow tied on the crown

explanation.surface: A fine ornament mounted on door locks.
explanation.definitionFit: A bun or bow of hair at the crown of the head is the topmost hair ornament.

clue.text: Crash Peugeot initially, leading to endless row

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word
endless cuts off the last letter

parts.note: a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: A Peugeot is first to lead into a crash after an endless argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives P; 'endless' cuts RANGE to RANG. A prang is British slang for a minor crash.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a car accident or bump.

clue.text: Provided with bed cover ?

parts.note: the bed is a garden flower bed, and its cover is a layer of compost or bark rather than blankets

explanation.surface: Given a bedspread.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners spread compost or bark over soil to protect it, giving the bed a covering.

clue.text: Someone quite near

parts.note: near reads as close by, but it also means stingy, tight with money

explanation.surface: A person close by.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightfisted person hoards money; near is old slang for mean.

clue.text: … Its purchaser hopes to be well covered

definitions.text: … Its purchaser hopes to be well covered

parts.words: Its purchaser hopes to be well covered
parts.note: well covered suggests plump, but the buyer of this policy wants protection for when they are not well

explanation.surface: A buyer hopes to put on some weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical policy pays for treatment, so its buyer is covered by it while staying well.

clue.text: Composer, heartless German confronting English in hostile state

indicators.note: in says the next pieces go inside the word for conflict

parts.note: war is a state of hostility

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its middle, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A composer, an unfeeling German, faces an Englishman in a time of hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves GN from German; with E it goes 'in' WAR. 'confronting' simply joins GN to E.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was the German composer of the Ring cycle operas.

clue.text: First performance about to be featured by Empire, maybe

indicators.note: something featured by another appears within it, so one piece goes inside
maybe says the letters of the word could be arranged differently

parts.note: RE is a Latin-derived word for about or concerning

explanation.surface: An opening night is about to be shown at the Empire cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges the cinema's name to PMIERE, and 'featured by' sets the about word inside after the P. The Empire is a common name for British theatres and cinemas.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening night of a play or film is its debut showing.
